clue.text: Commissions scarf for a worse than useless supporter

parts.note: commissions are jobs of work given to someone
a comforter is a woollen scarf

explanation.surface: Someone is paid to supply a scarf for a fan who is no help at all.
explanation.walkthrough: JOB'S COMFORTER comes from the Book of Job, whose friends made his suffering worse while claiming to console him.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a person whose attempts at consolation only deepen the misery, so their support does harm.

clue.text: Broke an order and behaved selfishly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pushed in ahead of people waiting in line
second meaning: put oneself before others' turn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke an order' sounds like disobeying a command; here the order is a line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing ahead in a line disrupts its sequence, and doing so is the classic act of putting oneself first.

clue.text: Poet is feeling passionate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Robert ..., Scotland's national poet
second meaning: glows with strong emotion

explanation.surface: A poet is in the grip of strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns wrote Auld Lang Syne, and someone who burns with desire is aflame with emotion.

clue.text: White Paper that shows no conviction?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blank page with nothing written on it
second meaning: a criminal record with no offences on it

explanation.surface: A government policy document seems to lack any firm commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: A White Paper is a British government policy document; here it is simply unmarked paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank page and a spotless record both have no marks recorded against them.

clue.text: Soft colour for a girl

parts.note: mild means gentle or soft
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A gentle shade is chosen for a little girl's room.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a traditional English female first name, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Men tied in with network?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: elderly men, in the informal phrase for an old chap
second meaning: former pupils sharing the school tie and its web of contacts

explanation.surface: Some men are caught up in a shadowy web of connections.
explanation.walkthrough: The old school tie is the emblem of the informal network of influence among former pupils of British public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual term for elderly chaps and the name for former pupils bound by their school's network of favours.

clue.text: Error of sort where O replaces E?

indicators.note: spells out that one letter is swapped for another in the word

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: A printing mistake in which one vowel has been set instead of another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nearly describes itself: swapping a letter is exactly such a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing mistake.

clue.text: Special article about record — provide copy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
special treatment of the word reworks it into something different

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a feature about an achievement and files it.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to reproduce or duplicate, making a copy.

clue.text: Finished the second part of flight in disarray

parts.note: all over means finished
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
a hop is a short stage of a journey by air

explanation.surface: A flight's second leg ended in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second' looks like an ordinal; it is THE plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means scattered everywhere, completely disorganised.

clue.text: Poet's editor was amazed

parts.note: Andrew Marvell, the seventeenth-century English poet; the 's means 'has'
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A poet's editor was astonished by the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To marvel is to wonder at something, so the past tense matches being astonished.

clue.text: Youngster, one learner taken on

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, and informally a cheeky youngster
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A youngster has been accepted as a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces join in order, each taken on after the last, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a young person enrolled to be taught, someone a school or tutor has accepted for instruction.

clue.text: Half the things needed for European city

indicators.note: only half of the phrase's word is kept, the back half being thrown away

parts.note: essentials are things that are needed

explanation.surface: Only half the necessary supplies are available for a trip to a continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSENTIALS has ten letters; the first five give ESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Bird cornered and unable to move, initially

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a black crow-like bird

definitions.text: cornered and unable to move, initially
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the chess piece that starts in a corner square, boxed in until other pieces move

explanation.surface: A bird is trapped in a corner and cannot fly off at first.
explanation.walkthrough: At the start of a chess game each of these pieces sits in a corner, hemmed in by the knight and pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gregarious black corvid and the castle piece in chess.

clue.text: Organisation behind spy ring so long

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency running spies
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: An agency running an espionage ring bids farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an Italian informal goodbye, matching the casual farewell phrase.

clue.text: Where to take chances with wheels, as rally's ending

definitions.text: Where to take chances with wheels
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Monaco resort whose casino has roulette wheels
second meaning: the finishing town of the classic motor rally named after it

explanation.walkthrough: The wheels look like car wheels for a rally, but in the first meaning they are roulette wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco resort is famed for its casino gambling and as the finishing point of a classic motor rally.

clue.text: Moved off one's trolley

definitions.meaning: first meaning: emotionally affected
second meaning: slightly mad, from a British idiom for crazy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved off' reads as stepping away from a trolley, but the clue splits after 'Moved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched means both emotionally stirred and a little crazy, as is off one's trolley in British slang.

clue.text: A French picture ruler is taking apart

parts.note: un is French for a
pic is short for picture
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A French portrait of a monarch is being dismantled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpicking means undoing stitches, so dismantling something piece by piece.

clue.text: Soldiers in coach keeping place for reserves

indicators.note: the coach keeps the soldiers, holding them within it

parts.note: short for stagecoach
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops travel in a coach that carries a spare supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is space where spare supplies are kept until wanted.

clue.text: Not stopping to speak

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fast, like a train that skips stations
second meaning: to put into words

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests talking without pause; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An express service runs without intermediate halts, and to express a thought is to voice it.

clue.text: Easy game, say, to support

indicators.note: say asks us to go by how the words are spoken, not written

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person, easy game for a swindler

explanation.surface: A soft target is offered help.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help and comfort given in time of need.

clue.text: Job description, in the case of a doctor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what Job was, the biblical byword for long-suffering endurance

definitions.text: in the case of a doctor
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person a doctor treats, a medical case

explanation.surface: A doctor's job description is under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: Job with a capital J is the Old Testament figure, proverbially enduring; the surface hides him as a job of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes biblical Job's endurance, and the noun means someone under medical treatment.

clue.text: Make the best of a tense possibility

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring to the ideal state
second meaning: a grammatical tense, as in I have done

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to make the most of a nervy situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervy, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to refine flawlessly, and it also names one of the verb tenses in grammar.

clue.text: Very strange Scots

definitions.meaning: first meaning: extremely, as an adverb in Scottish dialect
second meaning: odd or unfamiliar, in Scottish dialect

explanation.surface: Scottish people are described as rather peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' says both meanings are Scottish words, not that the definition is about Scotland's people.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish dialect unco serves as an intensifier meaning extremely and as an adjective meaning unusual.

clue.text: Lasting effect of damage by second vehicle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A second car caused damage with lasting consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left behind after a wound or injury heals.

clue.text: Give hiding to, making many feel pain

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to ache is to feel pain

explanation.surface: A beating causes a lot of people to suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give hiding to' sounds like a thrashing, but it means put in a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache something is to stow it in a secret place, giving it concealment.

clue.text: Ring family before midnight

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: the middle of the word is what is kept, a single central letter

parts.note: read as the mid of night, its central letter

explanation.surface: A family rings in before the stroke of twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is the loud ringing sound of struck metal, such as a bell.

clue.text: Colour from factory finally put in tin

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of factory

explanation.surface: Paint from the works is packed into tins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue shade, one of the printer's primary colours.

clue.text: Make one run if you take part

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is taken, the letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters straddle the three words

explanation.surface: An invitation to join in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify things is to bring them together into a single whole.

clue.text: In relation to ringleader, a head appears to go too far

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: read as the leader of ring, its opening letter
so much a head means so much each

explanation.surface: A gang's ringleader seems to be overstepping the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' must be split into ring and leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to stretch beyond one's limits or aim too high.

clue.text: Difference of attitudes in Dombey and Son, say

definitions.text: Difference of attitudes in Dombey and Son, say

parts.words: Difference of attitudes in Dombey and Son, say
parts.note: surface reading: a clash of outlooks between characters in the Dickens novel
setter's reading: in the title the word 'and' is the space separating father from son

explanation.surface: A critic remarks on the clash between father and son in Dickens's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The title puts father and son on either side of 'and', the space between one age group and the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the difference in values and outlook between parents and their children.
